title: Mitten State & The Midwest
description: 4 rounds and a final wager on Michigan, metro Detroit, and the greater Midwest — coneys, Motown, muscle, and 1 gentle jab at Ohio.

questions.prompt: In The Wizard of Oz, Dorothy's farmhouse gets whisked away from which state?
questions.answer_note: source: L. Frank Baum's novel and MGM's 1939 film — Dorothy Gale lives on a Kansas farm.

questions.prompt: Detroit's most famous coney rivalry pits Lafayette Coney Island against which next-door neighbor?
questions.answer_note: source: Detroit Historical Society — American (est. 1917) and Lafayette have shared the same W. Lafayette Blvd block for a century.

questions.prompt: The classic mnemonic HOMES helps you remember which 5 things?
questions.answer_note: source: EPA Great Lakes atlas — Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, Superior.

questions.prompt: To drive from downtown Detroit into Windsor, Canada, you head south.
questions.answer_note: source: USGS maps — Windsor, Ontario sits due south of Detroit, across the Detroit River.

questions.prompt: Detroit's beloved Vernors is what flavor of soda?
questions.answer_note: source: Vernors (Keurig Dr Pepper) — Vernors is a barrel-aged ginger ale born in Detroit.

questions.prompt: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame opened in 1995 in which Great Lakes city?
questions.answer_note: source: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame — the museum opened on Cleveland's Lake Erie shore in September 1995.

questions.prompt: The 1987 film RoboCop patrols a dystopian future version of which city?
questions.answer_note: source: Orion Pictures — RoboCop is set in a crime-ridden, near-future 'Old Detroit.'

questions.prompt: Which Detroit team won back-to-back 1989 and 1990 championships as the 'Bad Boys'?
questions.answer_note: source: NBA — the 'Bad Boys' Pistons took the 1989 and 1990 NBA Finals.

questions.prompt: The Mall of America opened in 1992 in which state?
questions.answer_note: source: City of Bloomington, Minnesota — the mega-mall opened just outside Minneapolis in 1992.

questions.prompt: The University of Michigan was founded in 1817 — 20 years before statehood — in which city?
questions.answer_note: source: University of Michigan — founded 1817 in Detroit as the Catholepistemiad; it moved to Ann Arbor in 1837.

questions.prompt: Legendary investor Warren Buffett is 'the Oracle of' which Midwest city?
questions.answer_note: source: Berkshire Hathaway — Buffett has lived and invested from Omaha, Nebraska since the 1950s.

questions.prompt: Faygo's iconic Redpop is what flavor?
questions.answer_note: source: Faygo Beverages, Detroit since 1907 — Redpop is its famous strawberry soda.

questions.prompt: In what year did Ford's Model T first go on sale?
questions.answer_note: source: Ford Motor Co. — the first Model T rolled out of Detroit's Piquette Avenue plant in 1908.

questions.prompt: Which future president grew up in Grand Rapids and snapped the ball for Michigan's football team?
questions.answer_note: source: Gerald R. Ford Presidential Library — Ford played center for the Wolverines, 1932-34.

questions.prompt: Historic Route 66 began its 2,448-mile run to Santa Monica in which Midwest city?
questions.answer_note: source: National Park Service Route 66 program — the Mother Road's eastern terminus was Chicago.

questions.prompt: Every US state flies a rectangular flag.
questions.answer_note: source: Ohio Revised Code — Ohio's swallowtail 'burgee' is the only non-rectangular state flag. Even their flag cuts a corner.

questions.prompt: Minneapolis and St. Paul face each other across which river?
questions.answer_note: source: USGS — the Twin Cities grew up on opposite banks of the upper Mississippi River.

questions.prompt: Which state has stamped 'America's Dairyland' on its license plates since 1940?
questions.answer_note: source: Wisconsin DOT — the slogan joined Wisconsin plates in 1940 and never left.

questions.prompt: Motown legend Stevie Wonder was born in which Michigan city?
questions.answer_note: source: Britannica — Stevie Wonder was born in Saginaw in 1950; his family moved to Detroit when he was 4.

questions.prompt: The 1984 Tigers started the season 35-5, then won the World Series over which team?
questions.answer_note: source: MLB — Detroit beat the San Diego Padres 4 games to 1; the Cubs had fallen to San Diego in the NLCS.

questions.prompt: FDR's call for an 'Arsenal of Democracy' became the WWII nickname of which US city?
questions.answer_note: source: FDR's December 1940 fireside chat — Detroit's converted auto plants armed the Allies.

questions.prompt: In feet, how tall is the Gateway Arch in St. Louis?
questions.answer_note: source: National Park Service — the Arch stands 630 feet tall and exactly 630 feet wide.

questions.prompt: Immortalized in a 1976 Gordon Lightfoot ballad, the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald sank on which Great Lake?
questions.answer_note: source: NOAA — the Fitzgerald went down in a Lake Superior storm on November 10, 1975, with all 29 crew.

questions.prompt: Tim Allen's sitcom Home Improvement, with its 'Tool Time' show, was set in which metro area?
questions.answer_note: source: ABC (1991-99) — the Taylors lived in suburban Detroit, Lions and Wings jokes included.

questions.prompt: In Cincinnati, a '3-way' is chili, shredded cheese, and what underneath?
questions.answer_note: source: Cincinnati's Empress chili parlors, since 1922 — a 3-way is spaghetti, chili, and a pile of cheddar.

questions.prompt: At its WWII peak, Ford's Willow Run plant finished 1 what per hour?
questions.answer_note: source: The Henry Ford — Willow Run hit 'a bomber an hour,' building 8,685 B-24 Liberators.

questions.prompt: Lake Superior lies entirely within the United States.
questions.answer_note: source: EPA — Superior straddles the Canadian border; Lake Michigan is the only all-American Great Lake.

questions.prompt: 'If you build it, he will come.' The 1989 film Field of Dreams is set in which state?
questions.answer_note: source: Universal Pictures — the movie was shot on a Dyersville, Iowa farm that fans still visit.

questions.prompt: Schlitz, Pabst, and Miller all rose to fame brewing in which Midwest city?
questions.answer_note: source: Milwaukee County Historical Society — Schlitz was literally 'the beer that made Milwaukee famous.'

questions.prompt: The 'Belleville Three' — Atkins, May, and Saunderson — pioneered which music genre in 1980s metro Detroit?
questions.answer_note: source: Detroit Historical Museum — 3 Belleville schoolmates invented techno; house music belongs to Chicago.

questions.prompt: Which former featherweight boxer and auto-plant worker founded Motown Records in 1959?
questions.answer_note: source: Motown Museum — Berry Gordy Jr. launched the label with an $800 family loan at 2648 W. Grand Blvd.

questions.prompt: Miners from which corner of Britain brought the pasty to the Upper Peninsula?
questions.answer_note: source: Michigan Tech archives — Cornish miners packed pasties into UP copper and iron mines in the 1840s.

questions.prompt: In what year did the Mackinac Bridge first open to traffic?
questions.answer_note: source: Mackinac Bridge Authority — the 5-mile span opened November 1, 1957, uniting the 2 peninsulas.

questions.prompt: Which Lansing native won the 1979 NCAA title with Michigan State before 5 NBA rings?
questions.answer_note: source: NCAA/NBA — Magic Johnson beat Larry Bird's Indiana State in the 1979 final, then won 5 titles with the Lakers.

questions.prompt: The 1955 Montgomery bus where Rosa Parks kept her seat is displayed in which Michigan city?
questions.answer_note: source: The Henry Ford, Dearborn — the museum restored the actual bus; Parks spent her later life in Detroit.

questions.prompt: Before Kitty Hawk, Wilbur and Orville Wright built their flyers in a bike shop in which Ohio city?
questions.answer_note: source: NPS Dayton Aviation Heritage — the Wright Cycle Company operated in Dayton. Credit where due, Ohio.

questions.prompt: That '70s Show was set in the fictional town of Point Place, Wisconsin.
questions.answer_note: source: Fox (1998-2006) — the Formans' basement sat in made-up Point Place, Wisconsin.

questions.prompt: In DC Comics, Clark Kent grew up in Smallville, a farm town in which state?
questions.answer_note: source: DC Comics — Smallville, Kansas has been Superman's hometown in canon since the 1970s.

questions.prompt: In 1909, a stretch of Detroit's Woodward Avenue became the nation's first mile of what?
questions.answer_note: source: FHWA and Michigan historical marker — Woodward between 6 and 7 Mile was paved as America's first mile of concrete highway in 1909.

questions.prompt: After the near-bloodless 1835-36 'Toledo War,' Ohio kept Toledo and Michigan received what consolation prize?
questions.answer_note: source: Michigan History Center — Michigan gave up the Toledo Strip for the western Upper Peninsula (the east was already its territory) plus 1837 statehood. The copper and iron say Michigan won.

questions.prompt: Battle Creek's cereal boom started at the Kelloggs' sanitarium. Which former patient stayed in town and launched a rival cereal empire in 1895?
questions.answer_note: source: Michigan History Center — C.W. Post, a Battle Creek Sanitarium patient in 1891, founded Postum Cereal there in 1895; Post cereals still bear his name.
